entries.violation_key: cancel_delivery(p_delivery_id uuid, p_cancel_reason text, p_performed_by uuid, p_idempotency_key text)
entries.justification: Re-reviewed live pg_get_functiondef 2026-10-20 (America/Chicago; read 2026-10-21 UTC) after replay-binding batch 3b (20261019235000, ledger 20261021024020) put a wrapper in front of the renamed body. The public wrapper binds v_actor := auth.uid() in its DECLARE, raises IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REQUIRED without a key, refuses a NULL auth.uid() ('authentication required'), refuses a non-null p_performed_by that differs from v_actor ('actor mismatch'), and requires an active admin or sales_rep profile for v_actor BEFORE check_idempotency_intent can replay anything; it fingerprints auth.uid() as actor_id, never p_performed_by. It then passes p_performed_by (NULL or equal to auth.uid()) to the postgres-only _cancel_delivery_replay_impl_20261015, which repeats the same auth.uid() / mismatch refusals (its own message is 'ACTOR_MISMATCH: actor mismatch' since 20261102140000, ledger 20261102174004, which also refuses a completed delivery; re-pinned from live 2026-11-02), derives v_actor := COALESCE(p_performed_by, auth.uid()) (necessarily the caller), role-gates it again, and attributes every inventory, order, invoice, delivery, audit and activity write to that v_actor. The flag is predicate shape noise (the refusal compares v_actor IS DISTINCT FROM p_performed_by, with the parameter on the right, so the refusal-head pattern does not strip it), not an actor-forgery hole. The actor-forgery-fin-audit exception for this function was removed the same day: the new wrapper writes no financial_audit_log row and is no longer flagged there. Pins: the wrapper, the renamed body it delegates to, and auth.uid(); neither body calls is_admin()/is_sales_rep() (direct profiles role query), so no helper pin applies. Exception matches only the reviewed suspect parameter and exact function/dependency definition, owner, and effective EXECUTE contracts; missing or changed contracts leave the finding visible. Superseded review (2026-09-12, pre-wrapper body, md5 21da58c0c8f22d933ddd6938f5927194): same actor derivation and role gate.

entries.violation_key: convert_quote_to_order(p_quote_id uuid, p_performed_by uuid, p_idempotency_key text, p_expected_row_version bigint, p_below_cost_reason text)
entries.justification: Live pg_get_functiondef semantic review 2026-09-12, independently traced by RLS/migration reviewers for mutators and inspected by coordinator for the two read-only grouping reports. Public wrapper first invokes _begin_below_cost_money_write, which binds auth.uid(), rejects non-null mismatch, requires active admin/sales_rep; owner-only delegate independently repeats auth bind/refusal (13-17) before role/ownership checks (19-32). This is scanner noise, not an accepted actor-forgery hole. Exception matches only the reviewed suspect parameter and exact function/dependency definition, owner, and effective EXECUTE contracts; missing or changed contracts leave the finding visible. Reason-parser pin declined 2026-09-23 (CodeRabbit on PR #786), measured from the guard's own body: _begin_below_cost_money_write raises AUTH_REQUIRED on a NULL auth.uid(), ACTOR_MISMATCH on a non-null p_performed_by that differs from it, and INSUFFICIENT_ROLE unless the actor is an active admin/sales_rep -- ALL THREE before it ever calls public._below_cost_reason_from_json(p_payload), whose only effect is the text placed in the app.crx_below_cost_reason GUC. That call sits in the pinned guard's own definition, so the pinned digest already covers whether it is reached. The parser is IMMUTABLE SECURITY INVOKER, takes no actor argument, reads no table, and returns caller-supplied payload text the caller already controls, so no change to it can make forged attribution succeed; it is therefore not 'materially relied on in the semantic review' in the README sense. It also calls public._below_cost_reason_from_text, so pinning every transitive callee rather than every materially-relied-on dependency would expand to an unbounded closure. Pins are live database-side digests (definition+owner+ACL); none was invented here, because a wrong digest would un-match this exception permanently and turn the sweep red. Re-pinned 2026-10-28 (KNOWN_ISSUES KI-85): the sent-quote price lock (migration 20261027040000, #1105) re-emitted the private delegate after this review; the delegate pin now matches the live body measured 2026-10-28 (all three other pins were re-read and unchanged). The reviewed actor path is unchanged by that re-emission (auth.uid() bind, AUTH_REQUIRED, strict ACTOR_MISMATCH, active admin/sales_rep gate). This entry describes TODAY'S live body only, where conversion is still refused for anyone but the booking owner; a second entry below pins the candidate body of 20261027080400 for the controlled rollout/rollback pair.

entries.justification: CANDIDATE rollout contract added 2026-10-28 for migration 20261027080400_any_rep_converts_booking (PR #1165, not applied when written). Business decision (Mason, 2026-10-27): any active sales rep or admin may convert another rep's booking; the commission stays with the booking's own salesperson. Reviewed against the candidate delegate body, which differs from the current-live body only by removing the two NOT_QUOTE_OWNER ownership checks. Conversion is therefore NOT booking-owner-only under this contract: it permits every active admin or sales_rep, and it is the ACTOR ATTRIBUTION that stays bound. The delegate still binds v_actor := auth.uid(), raises AUTH_REQUIRED on NULL, raises ACTOR_MISMATCH when p_performed_by IS DISTINCT FROM that actor, and refuses anyone who is not an active admin or sales_rep (INSUFFICIENT_ROLE: drivers and switched-off users stay refused), all before any write; the public wrapper first runs _begin_below_cost_money_write, which repeats the bind and the role gate. So a forged actor is still refused and the actor recorded is always the authenticated caller. This is scanner noise, not an accepted actor-forgery hole. This entry and the current-live entry above are a controlled rollout and rollback pair for the same scanner exception: the live entry matches only today's body, this one matches only the exact candidate body, and both pin every material dependency (auth.uid(), the guard helper, the private delegate, the public wrapper) by definition, owner and effective EXECUTE grants, so any other body, role, grant or owner leaves the finding visible. The candidate delegate digest was captured from actual execution in a disposable PostgreSQL replica (Supabase postgres 17.6.1.143, live schema baseline restored, every later migration replayed, candidate applied) using the sweep's own contract expression, after the same replica first reproduced all sixteen live contract digests of the reviewed functions exactly; it was not typed in or edited by hand.
